rule: GOAL: Fill four empty slots in the box to match the color sequence shown at the top of the screen. CONTROLS: Click a color in the bottom palette to select it, then click a slot in the box to place it. RULE: Colors must be placed in the exact left-to-right order displayed in the reference row above the box. TRAP: Believing the top row was just decoration rather than the mandatory target sequence caused unnecessary experimentation with wrong colors.

GOAL: Navigate the blue block from the top-left start to the bottom-right exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block exactly one grid cell per press. RULE: The level is cleared upon reaching the goal cell. TRAP: Moving one pixel at a time wastes actions; each key press shifts the whole coarse cell.

GOAL: Catch the falling block on the moving blue platform to prevent it from hitting the ground. CONTROLS: Left and Right arrows shift the platform horizontally; Spacebar drops the block. RULE: The block only survives if it lands directly on the platform's surface. TRAP: Thinking the block bounces off walls; it simply vanishes if it misses the platform entirely.

GOAL: Move the purple square to touch the ball. CONTROLS: Clicking a nearby spot moves the square toward it. RULE: The square only moves if the click is within six steps. TRAP: Believing you can click far away to move quickly wastes turns.

GOAL: Move the yellow key to the yellow slot in the wall. CONTROLS: Click the key, then click the target slot. RULE: The key only moves when dragged from its start to the lock. TRAP: Clicking the key alone does nothing; you must specify a destination.

GOAL: Slide the key right into the matching slot. CONTROLS: Down moves the key right; Left moves it left. RULE: The key rides the edge of the gray band, so align its tip with the target column. TRAP: Assuming the key floats freely; it actually pushes the gray boundary, shrinking the white space behind it.

GOAL: Match each slot's color to the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP or DOWN cycles the current slot's color. RULE: Cycle through all seven colors to find the correct one for each column. TRAP: Assuming UP and DOWN both move forward in the sequence, doubling your clicks unnecessarily.

GOAL: Make the ball drop exactly into the socket at the bottom. CONTROLS: Click vertical switches to change drop distance; click the ball to start the drop. RULE: The number of lit vertical switches determines how far the ball falls. TRAP: Horizontal switches are distractions; only vertical switches affect the ball's path.

GOAL: Push one crate into the target slot. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; Space absorbs or drops a held crate. RULE: You must stand adjacent to the crate, facing it, to pick it up. TRAP: Pressing a direction into an obstacle blocks movement but does not rotate your facing.

GOAL: Sort tokens by color into their matching boxes. CONTROLS: Click a token to select it, click a destination to swap, and press space to submit. RULE: Slots follow a fixed sequence where red tokens occupy the ends and green tokens fill the middle. TRAP: Assuming slot order matches visual layout wastes time; the actual order is red, green, red.

GOAL: Raise the lowest water band to the top by managing flow between layers. CONTROLS: Clicking a boundary moves water from the lower band to the upper one. RULE: A click fails if the source band is empty or the destination is already full. TRAP: Believing water is conserved; it is created when rising, but requires an available source to flow.

GOAL: Place letters so the sequence reads correctly from left to right. CONTROLS: Click palette colors to fill empty slots; press space to submit. RULE: Letters inside colored boxes count as a single block inserted at the pipe’s connection point. TRAP: Assuming all slots are independent; ignoring box grouping breaks the sequence order.

GOAL: Merge two pairs of blocks to create a yellow square. CONTROLS: Click a block to move it; click between two blocks to merge them. RULE: Merging requires clicking close enough to both blocks to combine them into a new type. TRAP: Assuming the merge radius is strictly eight pixels; the actual range is larger, allowing merges from slightly further away.

GOAL: Fill six empty slots with specific colors while installing a hollow frame. CONTROLS: Click a palette item to select it, then click a slot to drop it in. RULE: The hollow frame must occupy the third red slot before placing any solid colors. TRAP: Clicking the frame's hollow center does nothing; you must click its outer border to grab it.

GOAL: Traverse the corridor by using the lower loop to bypass the trap and reach the upper exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the character one tile in the pressed direction. RULE: The trap only activated when approached horizontally; entering from below was safe. TRAP: Assuming the trap was lethal from all sides caused wasted attempts to dodge it horizontally.

GOAL: Decode the pink glyphs to determine the correct sequence of seven yellow symbols. CONTROLS: Use arrows to shift the yellow symbol class in each slot until it matches the target. RULE: Each pink glyph uniquely maps to a specific yellow word, defining the required symbol class for that slot. TRAP: Assuming the initial yellow arrangement was close to correct; it was completely scrambled, requiring full realignment.

GOAL: Arrange colored tokens and frames to match a specific target sequence. CONTROLS: Click a piece in the tray, then click a slot to place it. RULE: Frames act as fixed separators, splitting the sequence into independent groups that must be solved individually. TRAP: Assuming all slots are interchangeable. Ignoring the frame dividers leads to placing tokens in the wrong section, breaking the pattern.

GOAL: Translate the eight-slot yellow row into the seven-slot blue row using the six legend pairs. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the cursor; Enter confirmed the glyph selection. RULE: Each yellow word maps to a blue word of a different length, forcing a unique segmentation. TRAP: Assuming one-to-one glyph mapping wasted time; the key was recognizing that word lengths changed between languages.

ESTABLISHED: The keypad displays a white plus pattern after interacting with the left panel. The right-side green bar decreases with every action, acting as a timer. FAILED: Pressing arrow keys, clicking keypad dots, and repeated left-panel clicks have not cleared the level or altered the validation state. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching the visible plus pattern on the keypad or clicking the purple dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys and mouse clicks trigger actions and reduce the timer. The left panel updates the keypad display but does not solve the puzzle alone.

GOAL: Sort colored items into matching boxes by placing frames in a red sequence box. CONTROLS: Click palette items to place frames and colors into empty slots. RULE: Frame order in the red box determines which color box fills each position. TRAP: Assuming boxes fill by visual position rather than frame sequence wastes moves.

GOAL: Guide the hero through a corridor to the exit while bypassing a lethal red trap. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the hero one step in the pressed direction. RULE: The trap kills anyone approaching from the side, but dissolves instantly if entered from below. TRAP: Believing the trap must be avoided entirely wastes time; it is actually a one-way gate meant to be passed from underneath.

GOAL: You must translate a coded message by matching words to their correct colored slots. CONTROLS: Arrows move your cursor between slots to place the right symbol. RULE: Each word length corresponds to a specific slot width, so match lengths carefully. TRAP: Do not assume slot counts are equal; different colors have different numbers of available spots.

ESTABLISHED: The arm extends horizontally to push blocks rightward. Vertical movement triggers a sweep-push for any block intersecting the band. Blocks stack in chains when pushed into each other. FAILED: Pushing the nearest block three times right caused a collision with the next block, blocking further movement. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving individual blocks to the far right edge without maintaining their specific relative order or connection to the arm. CONTROLS: Left/Right moves the head horizontally and pushes adjacent blocks. Up/Down moves the head vertically, dragging or sweeping any bloc

GOAL: Guide each colored bar to touch its matching cross target. CONTROLS: Clicking a bar extends it forward by a fixed step. RULE: The level clears only when all bars simultaneously reach their targets. TRAP: Thinking one bar reaching its target ends the level; you must complete all paths.

GOAL: Align the cross with specific grid markers to trigger completion. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cross three cells per press; Space activates or selects the piece. RULE: Movement is discrete and rigid; the cross jumps fixed distances rather than sliding smoothly. TRAP: Assuming continuous motion leads to overshooting targets; each press covers exactly three cells.

GOAL: Collect all blue dots using the blue plus shape while avoiding orange dots. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active shape; Space switched to the next shape. RULE: The plus covers its center row and column, so align the center to hit targets. TRAP: Assuming the plus covers a square area; it only covers a cross, missing dots near the corners.

GOAL: Align the yellow token with the fixed target marker. CONTROLS: Left arrow rotates the ring counter-clockwise; right arrow rotates it clockwise. RULE: Each click shifts every token one position in the arrow's direction. TRAP: Assuming the marker moves with the token wastes time; the target is static.

GOAL: Clear the board by reducing the remaining pieces to a single survivor. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, then click the valid landing spot to jump over an adjacent piece. RULE: Moves strictly follow orthogonal lines, jumping over exactly one neighboring piece into an empty space beyond. TRAP: Assuming grid coordinates match pixel centers directly, causing clicks to miss the intended landing cells.

GOAL: The level required moving the chain to the designated target area, not merely placing a single piece on the circle. CONTROLS: Clicking empty space shifted the entire chain; clicking an object swapped it with the white diamond; clicking the circle teleported the white diamond. RULE: The chain must align all its components correctly, not just the white piece, to satisfy the win condition. TRAP: Believing that getting the white diamond to the circle was the sole objective wasted actions on incomplete states.

GOAL: Cover three scattered dots at once using a moving line, an X, and a diamond. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; SPACE cycles control between the line, X, and diamond. RULE: Victory requires all dots to be covered simultaneously, not sequentially collected. TRAP: Believing dots disappear after a single pass wastes moves; they only count if covered in the final state.

GOAL: Match each panel’s red and blue cells to the pattern shown on its dial. CONTROLS: Click panel cells to toggle their color between red and blue. RULE: Dial letter W means the cell must be red; g means blue. TRAP: Thinking the dial updates live to reflect your clicks rather than showing a static target.

GOAL: You needed to rotate two yellow markers into their target slots. CONTROLS: Clicking colored arrows rotated specific grid rows or columns, moving markers along those paths. RULE: Rotating a row shifted all items in that line, allowing you to align markers by cycling positions. TRAP: Assuming arrow colors matched rotation direction was risky; always verify a move’s effect before committing to a long sequence.

GOAL: Match the panel to two dials by setting specific cells to orange. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggles its color between blue and orange. RULE: White dial segments mark cells that must be orange; green segments stay blue. TRAP: Assuming the entire panel needs one color; the dials define a specific, irregular pattern.

GOAL: Slide the two blocks to rest side-by-side at the divider’s base, forming a solid arch. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active block; merging creates a single wide unit that moves as one. RULE: The merged block cannot pass through gaps narrower than its width, locking movement to specific lanes. TRAP: Assuming the merge was permanent; the wide block actually splits when forced against an obstruction.

GOAL: Place both pieces onto the two separate rings to win. CONTROLS: Click a piece to activate it, then use arrow keys to slide it across the grid. RULE: Only the currently active piece moves; you must manually switch between them to position each correctly. TRAP: Assuming pieces move together or auto-switch; forgetting to re-click the second piece stalls progress entirely.

GOAL: Rotate colored glyphs to align their internal dots along the central vertical axis of each shape. CONTROLS: Left-click a glyph to rotate it ninety degrees clockwise; right-click rotates it counter-clockwise. RULE: The puzzle solves only when every dot rests in the geometric middle column of its respective color block. TRAP: Assuming the center dot is equidistant from all edges; remember the middle column has fewer pixels than the sides due to the dot's presence.

GOAL: Place orange and yellow pieces into their matching colored markers to clear the level. CONTROLS: Click left red to rotate pieces counter-clockwise; click right red to rotate them clockwise. RULE: Matching colors to markers is required, regardless of which specific piece ends up in which slot. TRAP: Assuming specific piece-to-marker assignments were needed led to unnecessary moves; any arrangement satisfying color match works.

GOAL: Decode a hidden image by determining each dial's correct rotation and color mapping. CONTROLS: Click dials to rotate their rings; toggle color inversion to define what white tiles represent. RULE: A white ring tile indicates the cell matches the dial's center color; gray indicates the opposite. TRAP: Assuming fixed color mappings without testing inversion leads to conflicts; the correct solution requires inverting specific dials.

ESTABLISHED: The dial rotates clockwise only when the block covers the center cross. Matching the dial to the box glyph alone does not win the level. FAILED: Moving the block away after matching the dial. Repeatedly covering the cross to cycle states without entering the dock. GOAL IS NOT: Simply aligning the dial symbol with the box symbol while standing elsewhere. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block. Covering the center cross advances the dial state. Uncovering it does not.

GOAL: Rotate the dial to match the box glyph, then push the block into the dock. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; covering the cross rotates the dial clockwise. RULE: Matching the dial alone fails; you must also place the block in the target box. TRAP: Thinking the dial state persists when uncovered; rotation only happens at the moment of contact.

GOAL: Set a 5x5 grid to satisfy four dial constraints using exactly 16 clicks. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell cycles its color between blue, red, and orange. RULE: Each dial dictates its ring: White marks cells matching the dial's center, while gray marks cells that must differ. TRAP: Assuming gray cells must be a single specific color caused paralysis; since only "not blue" was required, choosing any non-blue color satisfied the condition.

ESTABLISHED: The block sits at the top right. The red snake moves right then up, its tail vanishing as it goes. FAILED: Moving the block away from the snake’s path did not stop the tail from disappearing under the block. GOAL IS NOT: Simply avoiding the snake, as contact with the tail seems to erase it rather than cause failure. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block. The snake advances automatically each turn, shrinking from the tail end.

GOAL: Guide the yellow token to the center and orange to its target using only grid rotations. CONTROLS: Click red or green arrows to shift entire rows or columns left, right, up, or down. RULE: Arrows move all tokens in that line one step in the indicated direction, wrapping around edges. TRAP: Assuming arrows swap only two tokens; they shift the whole row or column, displacing others unexpectedly.

GOAL: Move scattered blocks into matching ring outlines across three rooms. CONTROLS: Click a block to select it, then use arrow keys to slide it. RULE: Blocks slide until they hit a wall or another block, so plan paths that leave no gaps behind. TRAP: Believing you can stop a block mid-slide; if you overshoot the ring, you must navigate around obstacles to correct it.

GOAL: Match the black shape to the yellow outline. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the black piece. RULE: The win condition required exact positional overlap with the yellow target. TRAP: Assuming pieces block each other; they pass through, so only final position matters.

GOAL: Insert the plug into the wall socket to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the plug up, down, left, and right. RULE: The plug's prongs must overlap the socket's prongs to snap into place. TRAP: Assuming you needed to stop adjacent to the socket; you must move into the occupied space.

GOAL: Match every cell’s color to its dial’s pattern while treating crosses as toggle tools. CONTROLS: Clicking a dial sets a target pattern; clicking a cross flips its four orthogonal neighbors. RULE: Crosses affect only adjacent cells, not diagonals or themselves, so plan toggles to avoid breaking fixed neighbors. TRAP: Assuming crosses constrain neighbors like dials, which wastes time checking impossible color matches on free cells.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking the red target toggles its rotation between two fixed states. FAILED: Clicking different cells on the red target yields identical results; no partial rotations exist. GOAL IS NOT: Forming a closed loop or connecting all pieces into a single chain. CONTROLS: Clicking the red piece rotates it. Clicking other pieces does nothing.

GOAL: Align the moving piece so its reflection covers the target zone. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the active object; Space switches control between the piece and the wall. RULE: The reflection’s position is calculated as the mirror of the piece across the wall’s center line. TRAP: Assuming the wall moves independently; it only shifts when active, altering the reflection axis for the piece.

GOAL: Split a block into a white top half and a purple bottom half. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selection box to a region; spacebar paints that region with the chosen color. RULE: Painting a region affects only cells matching that region’s geometric definition, not the visible shape. TRAP: Assuming the white wedge in the middle was part of the top half; it belonged to the bottom and needed separate purple filling.

GOAL: Navigate an 11x11 grid from start to finish using exactly 16 actions. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player two cells in the chosen direction. RULE: Movement requires both the intermediate and destination cells to be empty. TRAP: Assuming sliding movement stops at walls wastes time; strict two-step jumps are required.

GOAL: Slide the yellow block into the bar’s slot by shifting white and gray regions until they align perfectly. CONTROLS: Click blue squares to push boundaries; left moves top edge, right moves bottom edge toward fixed limits. RULE: Regions flow like liquid; they stop when hitting the bar’s left end or the screen’s right border. TRAP: Thinking clicks move the yellow block directly; they only shift the surrounding space, forcing the block to slide passively.

GOAL: Fill three target slots with boxes. CONTROLS: Arrows move and push boxes; Space picks up or drops a box. RULE: Carried boxes follow the player, allowing precise placement into tight spots. TRAP: Assuming you must push boxes directly into slots; picking them up lets you bypass obstacles and align perfectly.

GOAL: Move the block right to align under the green slot. CONTROLS: Left button pulls white from the first chamber into the middle; right button pushes middle white into the last chamber. RULE: Each push moves the block one step right but consumes middle white; refill the middle first if low. TRAP: Clicking push repeatedly without refilling the middle chamber wastes moves when white runs out.

ESTABLISHED: Moving right to column 45 triggers a major board shift. Mouse clicks on sky blue areas do nothing. Undo restores previous states. FAILED: Clicking specific wall or timer bar cells. Moving left after the shift. Repeated right moves from the starting position without reaching the trigger point. GOAL IS NOT: Simply standing at the right edge or clicking the blue background. The goal does not require clicking on white bars or black walls. CONTROLS: Left and Right move the player horizontally. Undo reverses the last action. Mouse clicks currently register but produce no visible effect

GOAL: Place white, purple, and orange cups into matching slots across the board. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cup, clicks select colors, space presses the cup down. RULE: You must manually change the cup color to match the target slot before pressing. TRAP: Assuming the cup color persists or that you can press without selecting the correct swatch first wastes turns.

GOAL: Rotate the L piece into a T shape, drop it into the gap, and slide it fully left to clear the level. CONTROLS: SPACE cycles the piece shape. ARROWS move the piece up, down, left, or right. RULE: The piece only rotates if the new orientation fits within the open space. TRAP: Thinking the budget bar resets or changes meaning when colors shift. It simply counts down; ignore the color change and focus on remaining moves.

GOAL: Balance water in five rooms to match target levels using pump actions. CONTROLS: Click pumps to move water between adjacent rooms. RULE: Water cannot flow over pillar tops, limiting room capacity. TRAP: Assuming intermediate rooms hold enough water to batch transfers caused delays; move water step-by-step to stay within tight capacity limits.

GOAL: Align the symbols to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the cursor; UP cycled the symbol. RULE: Each column held a unique set of symbols with fixed orientations. TRAP: Assuming all columns shared the same symbol cycle wasted time guessing.

GOAL: Guide the purple square along the dotted line to the blue circle target. CONTROLS: Clicking a dot moves the square toward it if within range; clicks outside range do nothing. RULE: The square can only jump three dots per turn, requiring step-by-step progression toward the goal. TRAP: Assuming you could jump further than three dots wastes actions on invalid clicks.

GOAL: Align three objects to specific coordinates by moving a wall, a U-piece, and a bar. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active object; Space cycles which object is currently active. RULE: Objects can pass through each other, allowing you to sequence moves so the wall clears the path for the bar to slide up. TRAP: Trying to position the bar first causes a block; you must lower the wall completely before moving the other pieces.

GOAL: Reach the exit without getting caught by the patrolling guard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step; pressing against the guard pushes it away. RULE: The guard only attacks when you enter its line of sight, not when you stand adjacent. TRAP: Thinking the guard is an immovable wall; treating it as a pushable block reveals the safe path.

GOAL: Catch falling ink on the bar to fill the container below. CONTROLS: Arrows move the bar horizontally; Space drops the ink. RULE: Ink flows left off the bar, so position the bar's left edge over the target. TRAP: Centering the bar under the spout causes ink to miss the target on the left.

GOAL: Deliver a yellow ball to the circle by merging four hidden magenta balls. CONTROLS: Click hidden dots to reveal balls, then click grid cells to slide them toward the center. RULE: Two magenta balls merge into one purple, and two purple balls merge into the required yellow. TRAP: Assuming the header color indicated the starting ball rather than the final target result.

GOAL: Capture three facing guards and reach the exit in nine moves. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player one step per press. RULE: Guards only lunge if you are directly in their facing line; approaching from the side is safe. TRAP: Thinking you must stay far away; you can walk right next to a guard if you are not in its ray.

GOAL: Click the mouse icon until the blue bar empties, then stop before it vanishes. CONTROLS: Clicking the mouse drains the bar; clicking elsewhere does nothing. RULE: The level ends when the bar is empty but still visible. TRAP: Waiting for the bar to disappear completely causes a game over.

GOAL: Align each column's pattern to match the target sequence shown above. CONTROLS: Left/Right arrows move the cursor between columns. Up/Down arrows rotate the current column's pattern. RULE: All columns cycle through the same fixed sequence of seven patterns, so the distance between any two is constant. TRAP: Assuming you must calculate the absolute shortest path for every column independently, rather than just cycling until the class matches.

GOAL: Arrange the four colored tiles to match the specific order shown in the top reference row. CONTROLS: Click a tile in the bottom tray to select it, then click an empty slot in the top row to place it. RULE: The solution requires matching the exact left-to-right sequence of the outlined target squares. TRAP: Assuming any arrangement of tiles that fills the slots is acceptable, ignoring the required color order.

GOAL: Grow two bars until they touch a cross shape. CONTROLS: Click bottom yellow to extend vertically; click right green to extend horizontally. RULE: Each click adds three units; stop exactly when bars touch the cross without overlapping. TRAP: Assuming bars overlap obstacles; they must touch but not merge, requiring precise stopping.

GOAL: Decode the cipher and set the answer dials to match the hidden pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the current dial through its sequence of shapes. RULE: Match each dial to the shape dictated by the decoded message sequence. TRAP: Rotating blindly wastes time; you must map the yellow-blue pairs first to know the exact target order.

GOAL: Center each cross so its arms cover all matching colored dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active cross; Space switches between crosses. RULE: The cross center must align with the geometric center of its dots. TRAP: Assuming moves are single-step; they actually jump three spaces per press.

GOAL: Decode a cipher by mapping yellow input sequences to blue output patterns, then align the result with the answer strip. CONTROLS: Arrow keys navigate the cursor to select specific wheel columns for adjustment. RULE: Match the yellow sequence to its corresponding blue pair in the reference dictionary to determine the required target pattern. TRAP: Assuming direct pixel comparison was sufficient; you must compare canonical class identities, not just visual heights or positions.

GOAL: Grow the key tip to its maximum size. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip; pressing aligns it with the lock. RULE: Transfers only grow the tip when it aligns directly over the lock panel. TRAP: Assuming alignment doesn't matter; misaligned transfers waste moves and shrink the key.

ESTABLISHED: The tail retracts fully, pulling red to the head where it docks. The panel indicator solidifies upon docking. FAILED: Attempts to pass the tail through the docked red block. GOAL IS NOT: Simply touching the red block once; it must be absorbed into the chain. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the head. LEFT retracts the tail. RIGHT extends the tail.

GOAL: Move the tip from the bottom of the shaft up into the handle to complete the tool. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip one step; the Transfer button teleports the tip up the shaft. RULE: The Transfer button jumps the tip over the narrow neck directly into the head section. TRAP: Thinking you must navigate the tip up through the thin shaft manually instead of using the jump.

GOAL: Arrange colored tiles to match the header sequence in a specific scan order. CONTROLS: Click a tile to select it, click another to swap them, press Space to submit. RULE: The pipe slot links two positions, forcing one tile to satisfy both checks simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming independent slots for all tiles; ignoring the pipe's shared constraint caused failed attempts.

GOAL: Arrange seven colored pieces into red, green, and blue slots to match a specific scan order. CONTROLS: Drag pieces from the bottom tray to their target slots, then press space to verify the arrangement. RULE: Linked slots count as one position, so scan the top row, then each box in order. TRAP: Assuming every visible slot is a separate check wastes time; linked pairs share a single validation step.

GOAL: Rotate the yellow block around the ring until it aligns with the selector slot. CONTROLS: The red arrow rotates the ring counter-clockwise; clicking a block does nothing. RULE: Only alignment with the fixed selector triggers completion; rotation direction is counter-clockwise. TRAP: Believing clicking the block itself moves it or that the arrow rotates clockwise wasted actions.

GOAL: Align the white diamond with the gray target, ensuring the connecting line avoids the ring's gaps. CONTROLS: Click a diamond to select it, then click an empty space to move the selected piece. RULE: The line is fixed between the two diamonds' positions, so moving one changes the line's path. TRAP: Assuming clicking the target swaps pieces directly, rather than requiring a select-and-move sequence.

GOAL: Read the hidden code to place letter tiles into red and green boxes. CONTROLS: Click to select a tile or frame, click a slot to place it, and press space to submit. RULE: The letter frame marks the column link, defining the left-to-right scan order for decoding the header. TRAP: Assuming the frame goes above the occupied green slot; it actually sits in the red slot sharing that column.

GOAL: Pass the key tip through the teeth to the socket. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the tip; clicking the middle column triggered the transfer. RULE: The transfer shrinks the tip only when it hits an obstacle. TRAP: Believing the transfer always moves the tip caused you to ignore the shrink mechanic.

GOAL: Align three orange dots onto the diagonal arms of the moving X shape. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the active shape; Space cycles to the next shape. RULE: The X’s center must sit at the intersection of the dots’ diagonal lines. TRAP: Assuming the diamond needed moving wasted time, as it already covered its red dots.

GOAL: Move two blocks through a shared maze until they meet and merge. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both blocks simultaneously; left and right inputs apply mirrored to each block. RULE: The maze is fully connected, allowing both blocks to reach any open space. TRAP: Assuming the maze layout was perfectly symmetrical, which caused incorrect path planning for the right block.

GOAL: Place six colored tiles into two linked columns to match a repeating header pattern. CONTROLS: Click tiles to select them, then click target slots to place them. Press space to verify the solution. RULE: Two adjacent red slots trigger a double scan of the blue column, requiring identical sequences in both passes. TRAP: Assuming each tile appears only once; the blue column is scanned twice, so its sequence must repeat exactly.

GOAL: Place the sliding block into the target box. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block one step in that direction. RULE: The block stops when hitting a wall or the box's solid interior. TRAP: Assuming the block could enter the box from any side; it only fits when aligned correctly.

GOAL: Arrange colored tiles to match a specific header pattern. CONTROLS: Click tiles to move them between trays; press Space to confirm. RULE: Tokens in specific slots trigger a double scan of the central group. TRAP: Assuming single-scan logic; ignoring the double-scan requirement for paired tokens caused misplacement.

GOAL: Place three shapes to cover all eight dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space switches selection. RULE: Shapes snap to a grid; only exact coverage triggers completion. TRAP: Assuming shapes could overlap or cover dots from any distance wasted time on impossible alignments.

GOAL: Guide all yellow dots to the red target zones. CONTROLS: Click row arrows to shift contents left or right. RULE: A dot locks in place once it enters a target bracket. TRAP: Assuming movement is global; shifts only affect the specific row clicked.

GOAL: Change the panel’s colors to match the pattern shown in its center mini-map. CONTROLS: Click individual tiles to toggle their color between blue and red. RULE: White spots in the center indicate which outer tiles must be red; gray spots mean blue. TRAP: Assuming the center is just decoration; it actually dictates the target solution for the surrounding grid.

GOAL: Move one cross to the far corner using a chain of jumps. CONTROLS: Click a cross to select it, then click a valid landing spot to jump over an opponent. RULE: A jump captures the piece in between, allowing continuous moves if the path remains clear. TRAP: Clicking an invalid target or a different piece deselects the current piece instead of moving it, wasting a click.

GOAL: Match the small pattern shown inside the two special tiles by filling the main grid. CONTROLS: Clicking a tile cycles its color through blue, orange, and red to match the hint. RULE: The two special tiles display the required 3x3 pattern for the upper and lower halves of the board. TRAP: Assuming the mini patterns were decorative; they are actually the direct solution key for the surrounding areas.

GOAL: Swap the yellow and orange blocks into their matching colored brackets. CONTROLS: Arrow buttons rotated two intersecting circular tracks of cells. RULE: Shared cells at the intersection allowed blocks to transfer between the left and right tracks. TRAP: Assuming the blocks stayed on their original track; they had to cross the intersection to reach the opposite side.

GOAL: Position three orange markers to form a triangle enclosing a clear central point, using a fourth marker as a temporary anchor. CONTROLS: Click a marker to activate it, then click a destination to move it, shifting the connecting strings. RULE: A move is valid only if the triangle’s center and all connecting lines remain free of obstacles. TRAP: Assuming a direct path exists; you often must move a marker to an intermediate spot first to clear the way for the final position.

GOAL: Turn all target tiles orange to match the hidden patterns shown in the mini-grids. CONTROLS: Click empty tiles to toggle them orange; click hint cells to reveal their coverage area. RULE: White pixels in a hint’s mini-grid mark the exact tiles that must be orange in the main board. TRAP: Believing hint cells themselves are targets; they are display-only, and clicking them wastes moves or causes errors.

GOAL: Rotate intersecting loops to align matching segments. CONTROLS: Arrows on loop edges rotate the entire vertical or horizontal ring. RULE: Clicking an arrow spins the whole loop in the direction shown. TRAP: Assuming arrows only move adjacent tiles; they affect the entire loop, so one click shifts many pieces.

GOAL: Align yellow blocks to top corners using arrow shifts. CONTROLS: Top arrows cycle the upper row; side arrows rotate vertical columns. RULE: Arrows only move blocks within their specific track, never across tracks. TRAP: Assuming arrows shift entire columns or rows at once wastes moves.

GOAL: Match tile colors to match the mini-panel indicators, using the center tile to determine the base color and the surrounding pattern to set the rest. CONTROLS: Clicking a tile cycles it through the available color palette. RULE: The mini-panel’s center tile reveals the target color for that specific grid cell, overriding other pattern assumptions. TRAP: Assuming the center tile is just decoration or a fixed reference; it is actually a playable target that must be clicked to match its own color.

GOAL: Flip the legend to match the target pattern, then retrieve the box. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block; moving onto the cross triggers a press. RULE: The gate only opens when the block’s current pattern matches the target. TRAP: Assuming the target is 6x6; it is actually a 3x3 grid, causing misreads.

GOAL: Guide the green piece to the yellow hub by bridging a gap. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece two spaces; clicks activated a red button to raise a connecting arm. RULE: The red arm only connects the lower path to the hub when vertical, requiring activation before moving. TRAP: Assuming the checker tile was an obstacle; it was actually a passable bridge needed to reach the hub.

ESTABLISHED: The piston retracts when the plug is uncovered. Reaching the valve cell does not trigger a win. The HUD icon order toggles, with a bar always under the blue outline. FAILED: Traversing the left corridor as the blue block. Reaching the valve cell. Pressing SPACE at the start or mid-corridor only resets position. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching the box via the left corridor. Simply standing on the valve cell. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block. SPACE resets position to the start. The piston position depends entirely on plug coverage.

GOAL: Align the plug's prongs with the socket terminals. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the plug; space rotated it. RULE: The prongs had to face the socket to connect. TRAP: Assuming rotation fixed polarity was wrong; position mattered more than orientation.

ESTABLISHED: The wall fully blocks passage; sliding stops at it. FAILED: Reaching the corridor end without smashing the wall. GOAL IS NOT: Simply standing next to the wall. CONTROLS: Selecting a token costs one action; moving slides until blocked.

GOAL: Position the black piece so its reflection perfectly overlays the yellow target on the opposite side. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the piece; each step updates the mirrored reflection in real time. RULE: The reflection mirrors across the center line, so moving left pushes the ghost right. TRAP: Thinking the black piece itself must touch the yellow target, ignoring the reflection mechanic.

GOAL: Paint the grid to match the hidden target pattern indicated by the mini-hints. CONTROLS: Clicking a tile toggles its color and the colors of its four orthogonal neighbors. RULE: The mini-hints show the required final state for the tile and its surrounding cross. TRAP: Believing the hints were static colors rather than instructions for a dynamic toggle mechanic.

GOAL: Align the floating piece and two walls into specific target positions to create a reflection. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active object; Space cycled which object was active. RULE: Objects pass through each other without stopping, allowing movement through barriers. TRAP: Assuming walls blocked the piece’s path led to unnecessary detours; direct movement was possible.

GOAL: Move the token from the left room into the right ring. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected token; clicks select it. RULE: Tokens slide through walls until hitting an obstacle or boundary. TRAP: Assuming the ring border blocks sliding; it does not, so the token stops short of the interior.

GOAL: Clear the path upward by removing the floor block directly above you to rise into the next room. CONTROLS: Left and Right arrows move your position horizontally; the mouse click targets and destroys specific blocks. RULE: You can only pass through walls by destroying the single green block aligned with your current column. TRAP: Assuming you can shoot diagonally or destroy blocks above your neighbors wastes moves; alignment must be exact.

GOAL: Advance the red piston to the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the blue block; horizontal moves count, vertical ones do not. RULE: The piston advances every fourth horizontal move, regardless of vertical detours. TRAP: Believing vertical moves reset the counter wastes time; they are ignored entirely.

ESTABLISHED: The reference shows a clean white-top, purple-bottom split. The wedge shape remains excluded from the block despite stamping attempts. FAILED: Rotating the stamper, pressing space, and stamping various triangular patterns did not clear the level or match the reference. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching the purple cell count (50/50) or placing the stamper icon in the preview panel. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the stamper orientation. Clicking the block applies the current ink color to the selected shape.

GOAL: Paint the block with red, green, purple, and orange bands by moving the cup and pouring colors. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cup to slots, clicks select colors, space pours the liquid, and clicking the cartridge applies its color. RULE: Pouring only changes cells if the liquid color differs from the current block color; matching colors cause no visible change. TRAP: Assuming the orange cartridge click failed; it actually worked but was invisible because the block area was already orange.

GOAL: Move the piece so its mirror image perfectly covers the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; Space toggles which piece is active. RULE: The line acts as a mirror; moving the black piece shifts the charcoal reflection oppositely. TRAP: Forgetting to toggle the active piece before moving the mirror line, causing the wrong object to shift.

GOAL: Fill the two yellow slots to clear the level. CONTROLS: One button shifts all items forward along the track; the other shifts them backward. RULE: Items cycle through a single fixed loop, so you just need to align their positions. TRAP: Believing items swap places or jump independently wastes time; they strictly follow the loop order.

GOAL: Paint the board using four colored regions defined by diagonals. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; Space applies the selected color; Clicks manipulate specific cup handles. RULE: Adjacent regions share a boundary line, meaning a single cell on the dividing diagonal belongs to both adjacent colors. TRAP: Assuming the dividing diagonal belongs to only one region caused failed fills; it actually belongs to both adjacent zones simultaneously.

GOAL: Paint specific board regions by pouring colored liquid from surrounding slots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block between slots; clicks select colors; space pours. RULE: Green fills the lower-left triangle; orange covers the bottom-right, including the diagonal. TRAP: Assuming a south slot exists wastes moves; the ring has only seven positions, forcing a longer path around.

GOAL: Move each token to its matching colored ring. CONTROLS: Click to select a token; arrows move it three spaces. RULE: Tokens slide freely through ring borders without stopping. TRAP: Believing ring walls block movement wastes turns trying to navigate around them.

GOAL: Match rotating glyph pairs to the specific symbols shown in the bottom answer strips. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor between panels; UP rotates the selected panel's wheel. RULE: Each panel displays a pair of identical glyphs; match the pair's class to the corresponding strip segment. TRAP: Assuming pairs could differ or needing exact rotation; only the shared class matters for completion.

GOAL: Match seven symbols by tracing dynamic portals that redirect sources between colored boxes. CONTROLS: Clicked slots to inspect contents; pressed space to confirm the final sequence. RULE: Tokens act as portals, rerouting subsequent mappings based on their current box location. TRAP: Assuming fixed slot-to-frame order; validation is sequential and stops at the first mismatch.

GOAL: Rotate the stars to align yellow segments and move the S-marker to the center. CONTROLS: Top buttons rotate stars clockwise; bottom buttons rotate them counter-clockwise. Side buttons shift the S-marker outward or inward. The center button swaps marker positions. RULE: Rotations affect the entire star ring, while side buttons only move the S-marker along its spoke. TRAP: Assuming individual segment rotation; you must rotate the whole ring to align colors, then adjust the marker’s radius.

GOAL: Slide the green block left and down to exit the maze. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block one step per press. RULE: Move the block until it clears the boundary. TRAP: Assuming the block must stay inside the visible ring; it can pass through border cells.

GOAL: Guide the key to the target slot. CONTROLS: Click buttons to raise water; click the key to push it. RULE: The gate opens only when water levels on both sides match exactly. TRAP: Assuming the key stays put as water rises; it actually floats upward, requiring precise timing to move it through the open gap.

GOAL: Place one yellow at the row's far end and another in the bottom block. CONTROLS: Arrows rotated the row and block; side buttons cycled a three-cell column. RULE: Park a yellow in the column to protect it while rotating the main row. TRAP: Assuming every move shifts all yellows, causing you to lose track of phases.

GOAL: Slide the plus piece into the inner ring using the green block as a pusher. CONTROLS: Arrows move the green block; pushing the plus piece slides it until it snaps to a ring alignment. RULE: The plus piece magnetically snaps to the nearest ring alignment when pushed, locking into place. TRAP: Assuming a single push moves the piece only one step; it actually slides across the grid until it hits the magnetic snap point.

GOAL: Clear level three in four moves by moving the yellow block to the second target. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move the nearest block one step toward the click. RULE: A click is ignored if two blocks are equally close or within the blast radius, causing a conflict. TRAP: Assuming the click only affects the closest block; overlapping influence zones cause no-ops, wasting turns.

GOAL: Merge two scattered pieces into one, then guide the result to the goal zone within a strict click limit. CONTROLS: Clicks move blocks toward the cursor; clicking between two close blocks merges them. RULE: Merges only work if both blocks are within a specific short distance of the click point. TRAP: Assuming all obstacles block movement; some decorative elements follow your clicks harmlessly, causing unnecessary avoidance.

GOAL: Slide the top wall down to uncover the hidden pattern. CONTROLS: Space selects the active wall. Arrow keys shift its position. RULE: Selecting a wall registers as a no-op if it touches the edge, blocking the next move. TRAP: Thinking the selection failed; it actually worked, but the guard blocked the subsequent move due to the previous no-op status.

GOAL: Create a specific color sequence by chaining boxes together. CONTROLS: Click a palette item, then click a box slot to place it. RULE: A frame inside a box directs the next color in the chain to that frame’s target box. TRAP: Thinking each frame must sit in its matching color box; frames must bridge different colors to form the chain.

GOAL: Move the player from the start to the exit while timing movements against a moving obstacle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step; waiting requires an invalid move into a wall. RULE: The obstacle blocks movement only when occupying the target cell; it does not kill on contact. TRAP: Believing the player dies if positioned above the obstacle; this false fear caused unnecessary detours and wasted actions.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking the bottom-red button cycles the yellow pieces through a specific path. The yellow currently sits at (51,36). FAILED: Guessing the path based on partial up-left movements without tracking the full cycle has wasted time. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching a specific coordinate once; the goal requires understanding the full periodic cycle of all yellow pieces. CONTROLS: Clicking bottom-red advances every yellow piece one step along its unique cycle simultaneously.

GOAL: Navigate a cursor across a grid to match specific target values on four parallel strips. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the cursor horizontally between slots or vertically to cycle through digit values in the current slot. RULE: The horizontal position strictly determined which digit strip you were editing, requiring precise navigation between columns. TRAP: Assuming digit cycles were identical across all strips caused wasted time; each column had a unique sequence length.

GOAL: Reach the exit without being hit by patrolling guards. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character one step in that direction. RULE: You move first, then guards move; never land where a guard will stand. TRAP: Assuming you can cross a guard’s path safely if you move first; you die if they sweep your landing spot.

GOAL: Reach the top exit while the orange guard patrols the right column. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; the guard moves simultaneously after each step. RULE: The red trap destroys itself if it lunges at you while you are in its target cell. TRAP: Thinking you could rush the exit; you must wait for the guard to clear the column first.

GOAL: Place three yellow gems into specific star arms, then trigger a swap arrow to align them with corner slots. CONTROLS: Click arm tips to shift gems outward; click star centers to rotate arms; click arrows to swap grid tiles. RULE: Rotations cycle arm positions while keeping the gem’s distance from the center fixed, requiring precise count to hit targets. TRAP: Assuming shifts work inward or that rotating a gem already in place helps; over-rotating or miscounting cycles wastes moves.

GOAL: Cover both lower targets with the two tetromino pieces. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece. Space switches the active piece between the two tetrominoes. RULE: The level ends only when both pieces are correctly placed on their respective targets. TRAP: The mirror line and upper targets are irrelevant; focusing on them wasted actions.

GOAL: Recolor two shapes to match the background by moving their centers to overlap target zones. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; Space switches between shapes. RULE: Any part of a shape touching the target area triggers the color change. TRAP: Assuming the center must land exactly on the target; arm tips also count for overlap.

GOAL: Merge two blocks into a single overlapping unit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active block one grid step. RULE: Success occurs only when both blocks occupy the exact same cell. TRAP: Assuming adjacent blocks count as merged; they must fully overlap to clear.

GOAL: Fill the two marked slots with yellow blocks. CONTROLS: Clicks rotate a row or column, or swap blocks between the center and side slots. RULE: Side slots are immune to row rotations, allowing you to park a block safely while spinning the main line. TRAP: Assuming every click changes the board state; clicking a side slot when empty does nothing, wasting a move.

GOAL: Align moving shapes to mirror a static pattern across a central axis. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the active piece; Space switches focus between the mirror line and the pieces. RULE: The mirror line reflects the current positions of all pieces in real time. TRAP: Assuming pieces must stay separate; overlapping them during movement is allowed and often necessary.

GOAL: Reach the goal while the timer bar lasts. CONTROLS: Arrows move you; each move drains the bar. RULE: The bar drains slowly here, allowing long detours. TRAP: Assuming a fast drain from previous levels caused wasted time.

GOAL: Maneuver a box carrying a cross to the board’s edge, then jump it over an enemy to win. CONTROLS: Click the box to select it; click the target ghost to execute the jump and capture. RULE: Boxes function as valid landing zones for jumps, allowing captures even when adjacent to the board boundary. TRAP: Believing boxes block movement entirely; they are solid obstacles but also valid destinations for crossing pieces.

GOAL: You must capture six enemies while dodging two patrolling guards in a grid-based maze. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character; each step counts toward your action limit. RULE: Enemies are captured only when you enter their cell, but only if your approach angle is perpendicular to their facing direction. TRAP: Do not assume guards move linearly; they bounce off walls, so memorize their full cycle to avoid fatal collisions.

ESTABLISHED: The right room's water surface is hard-capped by the ceiling at row 19, causing instant death if the player rises there. FAILED: Rising in the right room and attempting to move horizontally mid-ascent, as the rise completes before control returns. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching the right room's ceiling or surviving contact with the purple ceiling blocks. CONTROLS: Vertical rise is automatic and instantaneous; horizontal movement is only possible after the rise concludes.

GOAL: Clear the level in five moves by avoiding traps and patrols. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step in that direction. RULE: Traps only trigger if you step into their specific target cell. TRAP: Believing any adjacent step kills a trap; only stepping on its exact target works.

GOAL: Cover all yellow tiles using the piece and its reflections. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; Space cycles focus between horizontal line, vertical line, and piece. RULE: Mirrors reflect the piece across the line’s current position, so align lines first to position reflections correctly. TRAP: Believing mirrors move independently wastes time; they only shift when the piece moves, so position the piece after fixing lines.

GOAL: Move the falling block to the marked slot. CONTROLS: Arrows steer the block; Space cycles to other pieces or walls. RULE: Select the correct piece before moving; only the active piece responds. TRAP: Pressing Down at the bottom wastes a move, as it does nothing.

GOAL: Guide the X shape to cover all blue dots without disturbing the red diamond. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the piece one step; Space rotates the shape. RULE: The piece only interacts with obstacles if its diagonal tips physically touch them. TRAP: Assuming the entire bounding box matters, rather than just the four tip pixels, causes unnecessary pathing.

GOAL: Guide the player to the exit while dodging a dark-red chaser that lunges two cells per turn along its column. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one cell. RULE: Enter enemy cells from the side to neutralize them; the chaser only attacks straight ahead. TRAP: Assuming the chaser patrols a fixed path; it actually tracks your last position, so never cross its column again.

ESTABLISHED: Four markers exist. Moving a marker shifts a blob based on row and column sums. FAILED: Nine specific moves failed to clear the level within budget. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching coordinate fifty-three by fifty-five. CONTROLS: Clicking a marker selects it; clicking a destination moves the active marker to that spot.

GOAL: Reach the exit while dodging a relentless pursuer. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move you one square per turn. RULE: The enemy always moves closer to your current location. TRAP: Thinking the enemy moves after you; it moves simultaneously, so you must stay one step ahead.

GOAL: Guide the glowing dot to the target zone. CONTROLS: Click a marker to make it active; click a second marker to move the dot. RULE: The dot only moves from the currently active marker to the next clicked marker. TRAP: Clicking a destination without first activating its source marker does nothing, wasting a move.

GOAL: Align two line segments and two puzzle pieces to form a symmetrical pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; Space cycles focus to the next object. RULE: Identify the active object by locating its white highlight dots within the grid. TRAP: Assuming the cycle order matches visual layout; the pieces may switch order unexpectedly, requiring careful observation of the highlight to avoid moving the wrong object.

GOAL: Slide two blocks into the same spot to merge them. CONTROLS: Arrow keys push both blocks in that direction simultaneously. RULE: Blocks move until they hit a wall or another block, stopping just before. TRAP: Thinking blocks can swap places; they cannot pass through each other, so you must maneuver them into alignment carefully.

GOAL: Navigate from the start to the exit while evading a pursuing chaser. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player one step in the chosen direction. RULE: The chaser moves toward the player's current position every turn, always following the shortest path. TRAP: Believing you could outrun the chaser by moving directly away; you must use obstacles to break its line of sight or force longer paths.

GOAL: Group markers by color and move them into matching shells to form blobs. CONTROLS: Click a marker to activate it, then click its destination shell to move it. RULE: Markers must be surrounded by a white shell to be active; move them to shells matching their color. TRAP: Mistaking stray colored pixels in rings for actual markers, which lack the surrounding white shell required for activation.
